Reliability profile plot

Source: R/plot-profile.R
plot_profile.Rd

Plots the site reliabilities in order, with the informativeness and the mean reliability as horizontal lines; for a posterior fit, with the posterior interval of each reliability and of the informativeness. With type = "logit" the profile is shown on the logit scale, where the informativeness is the plain mean.

Usage

plot_profile(
  x,
  type = c("reliability", "logit"),
  centroids = c("I", "mean"),
  level = NULL,
  intervals = TRUE,
  max_sites = 60,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

An object of class reliability_profile, reliability_posterior, reliability_draws or reliability_design.

type

The plot: "reliability" (the default), the sorted reliabilities, or "logit", their logits as a strip.

centroids

The centroids shown as lines: any of "I" (the informativeness), "mean" and "harmonic".

level

Probability content of the posterior intervals, a number between 0 and 1. NULL, the default, uses the level of the fit.

intervals

If TRUE (the default), a posterior fit shows the interval of each reliability and of the informativeness.

max_sites

Largest number of sites to label, a positive integer.

...

Must be empty.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

A corner label gives the logit variance \(V\), the dispersion \(H\), the mean reliability minus \(I\) and the concentration count; for a posterior fit, their posterior means. The intervals of the reliabilities are the reliabilities at the quantiles of sigma_tau, because each reliability increases with it.

On the logit scale the profile of a posterior fit is taken at the posterior median of sigma_tau, where the informativeness is its posterior median. The logits there are \(\mathrm{logit}\, S_j = \log \sigma_\tau^2 - \log v_j\); their mean is \(\mathrm{logit}(I)\), and the bracket shows plus and minus \(\sqrt V\) around it.

Examples

prof <- reliability_profile(se = eight_schools$se, sigma_tau = 10, site = eight_schools$school)
plot_profile(prof)

plot_profile(prof, type = "logit")


fit <- reliability_posterior(estimate, se = se, site = school, data = eight_schools)
plot_profile(fit)
